title: He noticed why the sea looks blue - and became the first Asian ever to win a Nobel Prize in science.
caption:
He noticed why the sea looks blue - and became the first Asian ever to win a Nobel Prize in science.

In 1930, he won the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering what's now called the Raman Effect - how light scatters when it passes through a transparent material, revealing that material's molecular structure.

The discovery came from pure curiosity about something as ordinary as the color of the sea - and it's still used today in chemistry, materials science and medical diagnostics through Raman spectroscopy.

His Nobel wasn't the result of vast resources - it came from careful observation and a refusal to accept 'that's just how it is' as an answer.
